facts: The **top view** (or plan) is what you see looking straight down.
The **front view** is what you see looking straight at the front.
The **side view** is what you see looking from the left or right.

Each view is a flat outline. Include visible edges within it where appropriate; for example, a triangular prism's top view shows its ridge. Outlines can have straight or curved edges. Square grids are useful only for suitable cube arrangements.
steps: Choose the direction (top, front or side).
Imagine looking straight at the object from that direction.
Draw the flat outline and any visible edges within it.
